---
title: "Behavioral network optimization"
aliases: [behavioral-policy-optimization.html]
---

::: {#key-ideas .callout-note title="Key ideas"}
- The work policy defines the experience a network should learn from. The play
  policy seeks trajectories that contribute large gradients to that network's
  update.
- Work trajectories train the play policy; an importance-weighted mixture of
  work and play trajectories trains the target network.
:::

**Behavioral network optimization (BNO)** generalizes the behavioral policy
optimization algorithm of @papini2024. In their algorithm the target network is
the task policy itself. In BNO it can instead be a sensory network, a
[perceptual prior](computational-aesthetics.qmd), or another network whose
gradient can be estimated from trajectories. The **work policy** pursues the
extrinsic task; the **play policy** is the intrinsic policy trained to reduce
the variance of the target network's gradient estimate.

## Fit play from work trajectories

Let $P_w$ be the distribution of trajectories under the current work policy and
$G_\theta(\tau)$ the gradient contribution of trajectory $\tau$ for a target
network with parameters $\theta$. The gradient to estimate is
$\mathbb E_{P_w}[G_\theta]$. For finite second moments and a finite, positive
mean gradient norm, the unrestricted sampling distribution that minimizes the
sum of component variances is
$$
Q_\theta^*(\tau)=\frac{P_w(\tau)\|G_\theta(\tau)\|_2}{\mathbb E_{P_w}\|G_\theta\|_2}.
$$ {#eq-trajectory-proposal-fit}

Fit the play policy $\pi_{p,\phi}$, with parameters $\phi$, on work trajectories
by minimizing the forward KL divergence from $Q_\theta^*$ to the play trajectory
law $P_{p,\phi}$. With shared initial conditions and environment dynamics, only
action probabilities depend on $\phi$. The equivalent weighted log-likelihood
objective is
$$
\max_\phi\;\mathbb E_{\tau\sim P_w}\!\left[\|G_\theta(\tau)\|_2\sum_{t=1}^T\log\pi_{p,\phi}(a_t\mid z_t,h_t)\right],
$$ {#eq-weighted-trajectory-log-likelihood}
where $a_t$ is the work action, $z_t$ the perceptual latent, and $h_t$ the
agent's memory at step $t$ of a trajectory of length $T$. In the sample estimate
of @eq-weighted-trajectory-log-likelihood, one gradient norm weights the whole
action sequence. The fit need not realize $Q_\theta^*$ exactly: choosing actions
does not give the agent control over every outcome.

## Update the target from work and play trajectories

Collection alternates between work and play. The target network update uses
trajectories from both policies. With work fraction $0<\beta<1$, the trajectory
mixture is $M=\beta P_w+(1-\beta)P_{p,\phi}$. Each trajectory contributes the
importance-weighted gradient
$$
\frac{P_w(\tau)}{M(\tau)}G_\theta(\tau).
$$ {#eq-defensive-network-gradient}
The denominator is the mixture for the whole trajectory, not the probability
under whichever policy generated it. The work component makes the mixture
**defensive**: it covers every work trajectory and bounds the importance weight
by $1/\beta$. For a given mixture $M$, the expectation of
@eq-defensive-network-gradient under $M$ is the work gradient, even when play
visits different states.

This identity does not prescribe a collection schedule. If an implementation
reuses work trajectories that helped fit the play policy, their weights depend
on those same trajectories; the fixed-mixture identity alone does not guarantee
an unbiased update.
